summary: All 4 ACs verified. JsonFileStorageTest (7 tests) and GridSettingsTest (6 tests) are clean, well-structured, and follow correct PHPUnit patterns.
JsonFileStorageTest: uses sys_get_temp_dir() + uniqid() for isolation, tearDown() guards with is_dir() and glob() ?: [], LOCK_EX write is exercised by the underlying set() call.

GridSettingsTest: correctly uses InMemoryStorage test double to isolate GridSettings from I/O. Fluent API is verified by identity assertion (assertSame). Grid isolation test creates two GridSettings instances on the same storage with different IDs and confirms no data leakage.
phpunit.xml: both Settings and Storage suites correctly added. The All suite still picks up all tests via the tests/ directory.

No blocking issues. Two non-blocking suggestions noted: (1) inline tearDown cleanup in testDirectoryCreatedOnConstruct() could be fragile on test failure; (2) no coverage for the validateGridID() exception path in JsonFileStorageTest.

comments.note: NON-BLOCKING — testDirectoryCreatedOnConstruct() performs inline cleanup of the nested /nested/sub directories before tearDown() runs. If the test fails mid-assertion (before the inline cleanup), tearDown() will attempt rmdir($this->storagePath) on a non-empty directory, producing a PHP warning. Subsequent test runs are unaffected because uniqid() guarantees a fresh path. For robustness, consider a single recursive helper in tearDown() rather than inline cleanup, but this is an over-engineering concern for a test-only file.

NON-BLOCKING — JsonFileStorageTest has no test covering the validateGridID() exception path (i.e., passing an invalid grid ID to get() or set()). The normal code path is fully covered, but a dedicated test like testInvalidGridIDThrows() would complete storage-layer exception coverage. Low priority since DataGrid::__construct() is the primary guard.
POSITIVE PATTERN — GridSettingsTest correctly uses InMemoryStorage rather than a real JsonFileStorage, keeping the Settings unit test isolated from I/O. This is the right separation of concerns.
POSITIVE PATTERN — tearDown() guards with is_dir() before cleanup and uses glob() ?: [] to safely handle the false return when no .json files exist. Defensive and correct.
